argument:
MR D.I.Y.'s strongest purchase argument is cash-backed recovery and income: H1 cash after capex, lease principal and specified interest was RM462.958m despite declining earnings. A 17.71x trailing multiple and vendor-reported 5.32% yield provide a concrete starting valuation. Revenue growth of 6.46% and broadly flat operating profit preserve an operating base for cost normalisation.

This is not a debt-free retailer: lease-inclusive net debt is RM1.411bn. Dividends of RM511.784m exceeded the conservative cash surplus, and RM124.040m inventory release assisted CFO. Those limits warrant payout discipline, yet positive cash after lease servicing provides genuine recovery capacity. Quarterly margin contraction and weak technicals require patience. Upside would come from retaining sales growth while expenses stabilise, not assuming inventory releases recur or the dividend automatically grows.
key_points: Positive cash remains after capex, leases and specified interest.
17.71x earnings and reported yield offer a conditional recovery/income case.
Lease debt, inventory release and dividend overdistribution must remain explicit.
